q: In Python, what does len("Lahore") return?
e: "Lahore" has 6 characters.

q: In C, what is the value of 7 / 2 when both operands are int?
e: Integer division truncates toward zero, giving 3.

q: In Python 3, what is the result of 7 // 2?
e: // is floor division, so 7 // 2 is 3.

q: What is 17 % 5?
e: 17 = 5 x 3 + 2, so the remainder is 2.

q: In C, what is the result of: int x = 5; x += x++;
e: Modifying x twice without a sequence point is undefined behaviour in C.

q: Which data type is best for storing true or false?
e: A boolean holds exactly two values, true and false.

q: How many bits are in a byte?
e: One byte is 8 bits.

q: A signed 8-bit integer can store values from:
e: Two's complement 8-bit range is -128 to 127.

q: How many times does this loop print? for (i = 0; i < 10; i += 3) print(i)
e: i takes 0, 3, 6, 9, so it prints 4 times.

q: What does the break statement do inside a loop?
e: break leaves the nearest enclosing loop.

q: A function that calls itself is called:
e: Recursion means a function calls itself.

q: Passing by reference means the function receives:
o: The address or alias of the original variable
e: Changes inside the function affect the original variable.

q: In Python, what is printed? def f(a, L=[]): L.append(a); return L  then print(f(1), f(2))
e: The default list is created once and shared, so both calls return the same list [1, 2].

q: Which OOP principle hides internal details behind a public interface?
e: Encapsulation bundles data with methods and restricts direct access.

q: Method overriding happens when:
o: Two methods in one class share a name with different parameters
A subclass provides its own version of a parent method
e: Overriding replaces an inherited method in the subclass.

q: Method overloading means:
o: Same method name with different parameter lists
e: Overloading is compile-time polymorphism by parameter list.

q: In Java, a class can extend how many classes directly?
e: Java supports single class inheritance. Multiple interfaces can be implemented.

q: Which concept lets a parent-type reference call the child's overridden method at run time?
e: Dynamic dispatch selects the method from the actual object type.

q: A constructor is:
o: A special method that initialises a new object
e: Constructors run when an object is created.

q: In Python, what is "abc" * 2?
e: Multiplying a string repeats it.

q: In Python, what is "Pakistan"[1:4]?
e: Slicing takes indexes 1, 2 and 3: a, k, i.

q: In most languages, the index of the first element of an array is:
e: Arrays in C, Java and Python start at index 0.

q: What is the last valid index of an array of size n (0-based)?
e: Indexes run from 0 to n-1.

q: Accessing index 10 of a 5-element Java array throws:
e: Java checks array bounds at run time.

q: The finally block in try-catch-finally:
o: Runs only if an exception occurs
Runs whether or not an exception occurs
e: finally is used for clean-up that must always happen.

q: In C, memory allocated with malloc should be released with:
e: malloc and free are paired in C.

q: A memory leak happens when:
o: Allocated memory is never released after use
A pointer is set to NULL
e: Leaked memory stays reserved and cannot be reused.

q: In C, what does the & operator do before a variable name?
o: Gives the address of the variable
e: &x is the address of x.

q: In C, if int *p = &x; what does *p give?
e: * dereferences the pointer to get the value.

q: What is the output? x = [1, 2, 3]; y = x; y.append(4); print(len(x))
e: y and x name the same list, so x now has 4 items.

q: In Java, == on two String objects compares:
e: Use equals() to compare string contents.

q: Two nested loops each running n times give a time complexity of:
e: n iterations inside n iterations is n x n.

q: A loop where i doubles each time (i = 1, 2, 4, ... up to n) runs about:
e: Doubling reaches n after log2 n steps.

q: Binary search requires the array to be:
e: Binary search halves a sorted range.

q: Worst-case comparisons for binary search on 1,024 sorted items is about:
e: log2(1024) = 10, plus one final check gives about 11.

q: Linear search worst-case time is:
e: It may check every element.

q: Which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) worst-case time?
e: Merge sort is always O(n log n). Quick sort can degrade to O(n^2).

q: Which sort is best on an almost sorted array?
e: Insertion sort runs in near O(n) on nearly sorted input.

q: A stable sort:
o: Keeps equal elements in their original relative order
e: Stability preserves the order of equal keys.

q: After the first pass of bubble sort (ascending), the largest element is:
e: Each pass bubbles the largest remaining element to the end.

q: Push 1, 2, 3 onto a stack, then pop twice. What is on top?
e: Pops remove 3 then 2, leaving 1.

q: Which data structure is used for function calls?
e: The call stack stores return addresses and local variables.

q: The postfix form of (A + B) * C is:
e: Evaluate A + B first, then multiply by C.

q: Inserting at the head of a singly linked list takes:
e: Only the head pointer changes.

q: Finding the k-th element of a singly linked list takes:
e: You must walk k nodes from the head.

q: A binary tree node can have at most:
e: Binary means at most two children.

q: In-order traversal of a binary search tree gives keys in:
e: Left, root, right visits keys in ascending order.

q: The maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height 3 (root at height 0) is:
Searching an unbalanced BST built from sorted input takes worst case:
e: Sorted inserts create a chain like a linked list.

q: Which traversal visits the root first?
e: Pre-order is root, left, right.

q: In a max-heap, the largest element is at:
e: The heap property keeps the maximum at the root.

q: Average lookup time in a well-designed hash table is:
e: A good hash spreads keys so lookups are constant time on average.

q: When two keys map to the same slot, it is called a:
e: Collisions are handled by chaining or open addressing.

q: BFS uses which data structure?
e: Breadth-first search explores level by level with a queue.

q: DFS can be implemented with:
e: Depth-first search goes deep using a stack.

q: Dijkstra's algorithm fails when the graph has:
e: Negative weights break its greedy choice. Use Bellman-Ford instead.

q: A tree with n nodes has how many edges?
e: A connected acyclic graph with n nodes has n-1 edges.

q: Merge sort is an example of:
e: It splits the problem, solves halves and merges.

q: Dynamic programming is useful when a problem has:
e: DP stores sub-problem answers to avoid recomputation.

q: What is needed to stop recursion?
e: Without a base case, recursion never ends.

q: Recursive fib(n) without memoisation runs in roughly:
e: Each call branches into two more calls.

q: COUNT(*) counts:
e: COUNT(*) counts every row, including those with nulls.

q: To sort results from highest to lowest salary you use:
e: DESC sorts in descending order.

q: Which command removes all rows but keeps the table structure, usually fastest?
e: TRUNCATE empties the table quickly and keeps its definition.

q: What does SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks BETWEEN 50 AND 60 include?
e: BETWEEN is inclusive at both ends.

q: Which wildcard in LIKE matches any number of characters?
e: % matches zero or more characters. _ matches exactly one.

q: To test for missing values in SQL you write:
e: NULL is not equal to anything, so use IS NULL.

q: A candidate key is:
o: A minimal set of columns that can uniquely identify rows
e: One candidate key is chosen as the primary key.

q: A table is in 1NF when:
e: First normal form removes repeating groups and multi-valued cells.

q: 2NF removes:
o: Partial dependencies on part of a composite key
e: Every non-key column must depend on the whole key.

q: 3NF removes:
e: Non-key columns must depend only on the key.

q: The A in ACID stands for:
e: Atomicity means all or nothing.

q: A dirty read happens when a transaction reads:
o: Data written by another transaction that has not committed
e: If the other transaction rolls back, the read value never existed.

q: An index mainly speeds up:
e: Indexes speed reads but add cost to writes.

q: A student can enrol in many courses and a course has many students. This is:
e: Both sides have many, so a junction table is needed.

q: MongoDB stores data mainly as:
e: MongoDB is a document database.

q: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can fully guarantee at most two of:
e: During a network partition you must choose consistency or availability.

q: Which SDLC phase comes first?
e: You must know what to build before designing it.

q: The Waterfall model is best when:
e: Waterfall moves through fixed phases in order.

q: In Scrum, a fixed time-box of work is called a:
e: Sprints usually last 1 to 4 weeks.

q: Who prioritises the product backlog in Scrum?
e: The Product Owner owns and orders the backlog.

q: The daily stand-up in Scrum is mainly for:
e: It is a short daily team sync.

q: A user story usually follows the format:
o: As a [role], I want [goal], so that [benefit]
e: User stories describe value from the user's view.

q: "The system shall respond within 2 seconds" is a:
e: It describes a quality (performance), not a function.

q: "A student can reset their password" is a:
e: It describes something the system does.

q: Testing individual functions or classes in isolation is called:
e: Unit tests check the smallest testable parts.

q: Black-box testing is based on:
e: The tester does not look at the code.

q: Regression testing checks that:
o: Existing features still work after changes
e: It catches features broken by new changes.

q: For an input field accepting ages 18 to 60, boundary value analysis tests:
e: Bugs cluster at the edges of valid ranges.

q: Acceptance testing is usually done by:
e: It confirms the system meets business needs.

q: High cohesion and low coupling means:
o: Modules do many unrelated things and depend heavily on each other
Each module has one focused job and few dependencies
All code is in one file
e: This makes systems easier to change and test.

q: The Singleton pattern ensures:
o: Only one instance of a class exists
e: Used for shared resources like a configuration object.

q: The Observer pattern is used when:
o: One object must notify many dependents of a change
Algorithms must be swapped at compile time
e: Subscribers are notified automatically on change.

q: Which UML diagram shows classes and their relationships?
e: Class diagrams show attributes, methods and associations.

q: Which UML diagram shows messages between objects over time?
e: Sequence diagrams have lifelines and ordered messages.

q: Which command records changes in the local Git repository?
e: git commit saves a snapshot locally.

q: Which command uploads local commits to a remote repository?
e: git push sends commits to the remote.

q: A merge conflict happens when:
o: Two branches change the same lines differently
e: Git cannot decide which change to keep.

q: Which HTML tag creates a hyperlink?
e: <a href="..."> creates a clickable link.

q: Which tag is used for the largest heading?
e: h1 is the top-level heading.

q: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
e: alt text helps screen readers and shows if the image fails.

q: Which input type hides typed characters?
e: type="password" masks the input.

q: Which tag groups related form fields under a caption?
e: fieldset with legend groups form controls.

q: Which selector targets an element with id="main"?
e: # selects by id. . selects by class.

q: In the CSS box model, which is outermost?
e: Content, padding, border, then margin.

q: display: flex is used to:
o: Lay out children in a row or column with flexible sizing
e: Flexbox arranges items along one axis.

q: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
e: const cannot be reassigned. let can.

q: What is typeof null in JavaScript?
e: A long-standing quirk: typeof null is "object".

q: What does 2 + "2" give in JavaScript?
e: The number is converted to a string and joined.

q: === in JavaScript checks:
e: Strict equality does not convert types.

q: What is logged? console.log([1, 2, 3].map(x => x * 2))
e: map doubles each element.

q: Which method adds an element to the end of an array?
e: push appends. pop removes from the end.

q: A Promise in JavaScript represents:
o: A value that may be available now, later or never
e: Promises handle asynchronous results.

q: Which HTTP method is normally used to submit a form that creates data?
e: POST sends data in the request body.

q: HTTP status 404 means:
e: The requested resource does not exist.

q: HTTP status 500 means:
e: 5xx codes mean the server failed.

q: HTTP status 401 means:
e: The client must authenticate.

q: HTTPS adds which layer on top of HTTP?
e: TLS encrypts and authenticates the connection.

q: In a REST API, which method usually deletes a resource?
e: DELETE removes the resource at the URL.

q: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) happens when:
o: Untrusted input is shown on a page without escaping, so scripts run
A server runs out of memory
e: Escape output and use a Content Security Policy.

q: Which practice improves web accessibility?
o: Using only colour to show errors
Adding alt text and labels to form fields
e: Screen readers rely on labels and alt text.

q: Routers operate mainly at which OSI layer?
e: Routers forward packets using IP addresses at the network layer.

q: Switches operate mainly at which OSI layer?
e: Switches forward frames using MAC addresses.

q: Which protocol suits live video calls where speed matters more than perfect delivery?
e: UDP has low overhead and no retransmission delays.

q: The default port for HTTP is:
e: HTTP uses 80 and HTTPS uses 443.

q: The default port for HTTPS is:
e: HTTPS runs on 443.

q: Which port does SSH use by default?
e: SSH listens on port 22.

q: DNS mainly converts:
e: DNS resolves names like example.com to IPs.

q: DHCP is used to:
o: Automatically assign IP addresses to devices
e: DHCP leases IP settings to hosts.

q: Which address range is private (RFC 1918)?
e: 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16 are private ranges.

q: How many usable host addresses does a /24 IPv4 network have?
e: 2^8 - 2 = 254, minus network and broadcast addresses.

q: NAT allows:
o: Many private devices to share one public IP address
e: Network Address Translation maps private addresses to a public one.

q: The ping command uses which protocol?
e: Ping sends ICMP echo requests.

q: ARP is used to find:
o: The IP address for a domain
The MAC address for a known IP address
e: ARP maps IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses on a LAN.

q: Which device connects different networks and chooses paths?
e: Routers connect networks and route packets.

q: In a star topology, all devices connect to:
e: Failure of one cable affects only one device.

q: Which is the most secure common Wi-Fi security standard?
e: WPA3 replaces WPA2 with stronger protection.

q: Renting virtual machines from a cloud provider is:
e: Infrastructure as a Service gives raw compute, storage and network.

q: Using Gmail through a browser is an example of:
e: Software as a Service delivers a full application.

q: Horizontal scaling means:
o: Adding a bigger CPU to one server
Adding more servers to share the load
e: Scale out with more machines. Scale up with a bigger machine.

q: Which is an operating system?
e: Linux manages hardware and runs programs.

q: The kernel is:
o: The core of the OS that manages CPU, memory and devices
e: The kernel runs in privileged mode.

q: A process is:
e: A process has code, data, stack and a state.

q: Which process state means waiting for I/O to finish?
e: The process cannot run until the I/O completes.

q: A context switch is:
o: Saving one process's state and loading another's
e: It lets the CPU move between processes.

q: Which scheduling algorithm gives each process a fixed time slice in turn?
e: Round Robin uses a time quantum.

q: Processes P1, P2, P3 with burst times 24, 3, 3 arrive in that order under FCFS. Average waiting time is:
e: Waits are 0, 24 and 27. Average = 51 / 3 = 17.

q: For the same bursts (24, 3, 3) under SJF, the average waiting time is:
e: Order 3, 3, 24 gives waits 0, 3, 6. Average = 3.

q: Starvation in priority scheduling is reduced by:
e: Aging raises the priority of waiting processes over time.

q: A critical section is:
o: Code that accesses shared resources and must not run in two threads at once
The first line of a program
e: Mutual exclusion protects shared data.

q: A race condition occurs when:
o: The result depends on the timing of concurrent operations on shared data
Two programs use the same name
e: Locks or atomic operations prevent it.

q: Which is NOT one of the four conditions for deadlock?
e: The condition is NO preemption. Allowing preemption breaks deadlock.

q: The LRU page replacement algorithm replaces the page:
e: Least Recently Used approximates optimal replacement.

q: With 3 frames and FIFO, how many page faults for reference string 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2?
e: 1, 2, 3 fault. 4 replaces 1, then 1 replaces 2, then 2 replaces 3: 6 faults.

q: Which Linux command shows the current directory path?
e: pwd prints the working directory.

q: chmod 755 file gives the owner:
e: 7 = read + write + execute.

q: Which disk scheduling algorithm can cause starvation of far requests?
e: Shortest Seek Time First keeps serving nearby requests.

q: A hypervisor:
e: Examples are VMware ESXi, Hyper-V and KVM.

q: Ensuring data is not changed without authorisation is:
e: Integrity protects against tampering.

q: Which is an asymmetric algorithm?
e: RSA uses a public and private key pair.

q: To send a message only Ali can read, you encrypt it with:
o: A shared password in the email
e: Only Ali's private key can decrypt it.

q: A digital signature is created with the sender's:
e: Anyone can verify it with the sender's public key.

q: A hash function such as SHA-256 is:
e: You cannot get the input back from the hash.

q: Two-factor authentication combines:
o: Two different types of factor, such as a password and a phone code
e: Factors are something you know, have or are.

q: A fingerprint is which type of factor?
e: Biometrics are something you are.

q: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) assigns permissions to:
e: Users inherit permissions from their roles.

q: Ransomware:
e: Offline backups are the best defence.

q: A worm differs from a virus because it:
o: Spreads on its own across networks
e: Worms self-replicate without user action.

q: A Trojan horse is malware that:
e: Users install it believing it is harmless.

q: An email pretending to be from your bank asking for your PIN is:
e: Phishing tricks people into revealing secrets.

q: Following an employee through a secure door without a badge is:
e: Tailgating bypasses physical access control.

q: A firewall mainly:
o: Filters network traffic based on rules
e: It allows or blocks traffic by rules.

q: A VPN provides:
o: An encrypted tunnel over a public network
e: VPNs protect traffic on untrusted networks.

q: A man-in-the-middle attack is best prevented by:
e: TLS authenticates the server and encrypts traffic.

q: SQL injection is best prevented by:
e: Parameters keep data separate from SQL code.

q: In Pakistan, the main cybercrime law is:
e: The Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016.

q: Machine learning is best described as:
e: Models improve from examples rather than fixed rules.

q: Predicting house prices from features is:
e: The output is a continuous number.

q: Predicting if an email is spam or not is:
e: The output is a category.

q: Grouping customers by behaviour without labels is:
e: Clustering finds groups in unlabeled data.

q: K-means needs you to choose:
e: k decides how many clusters are formed.

q: In reinforcement learning, an agent learns from:
o: Rewards and penalties from its actions
e: It maximises cumulative reward.

q: Overfitting means the model:
o: Performs well on training data but poorly on new data
e: It memorises noise instead of learning patterns.

q: Underfitting usually means the model is:
o: Too simple to capture the pattern
e: Both training and test errors are high.

q: Precision is:
e: Of all predicted positives, how many were correct.

q: Recall is:
e: Of all actual positives, how many were found.

q: For a rare disease test, which metric matters most to avoid missing sick patients?
e: High recall means few false negatives.

q: Data is usually split into:
o: Training and test (and often validation) sets
e: Test data checks performance on unseen examples.

q: An activation function adds:
e: Without it, stacked layers act like one linear layer.

q: ReLU outputs:
e: ReLU passes positives and zeroes negatives.

q: Backpropagation is used to:
e: Gradients flow backward from the loss.

q: A learning rate that is too high can cause:
e: Big steps jump over the minimum.

q: Which network type is best suited to images?
e: Convolutional layers detect spatial features.

q: Transformers rely mainly on:
e: Self-attention relates every token to every other token.

q: Which search uses a heuristic plus the path cost so far?
e: A* uses f(n) = g(n) + h(n).

q: A decision tree splits data using features that:
o: Best separate the classes, e.g. by information gain
e: Gini or entropy measure split quality.

q: K-Nearest Neighbours classifies a point by:
o: The majority class of its k closest points
e: KNN is a lazy, instance-based method.

q: A large language model mainly predicts:
o: The next token in a sequence
e: LLMs generate text one token at a time.

q: AI bias most often comes from:
e: Models learn the patterns, including unfair ones, in their data.
